title: Monitoring open access publications at the SNSF: Challenges of open academic data
text: Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) expects grantees publish results funded research freely accessible format. meet expectation, grantees can choose gold green open access publication road. gold road involves publishing open access (OA) journal, green road relates publishing paywalled journal along upload simultaneously uploading article public repository. Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF) started OA monitoring publications resulting grants 2021. primary source monitoring direct reporting grantees provide SNSF publications. Access open academic data Crossref OpenAlex also important sources identifying unreported publications resulting SNSF-funded research. However, access closed academic data Dimensions also critical obtain broader representative picture SNSF-related publications. sources important SNSF OA monitoring, Dimensions remains largest source unique publications. analysis describes SNSF uses academic databases OA monitoring SNSF-related scientific publications highlights differences terms publications coverage open closed academic data, well challenges relying open academic data.

Note Since metadata recent publications always available reliable needed, SNSF OA monitoring delayed two years. example, means 2025 monitoring covers works published 2023. Accordingly, references “2023 OA monitoring” refer publications 2023.

title: Monitoring open access publications at the SNSF: Challenges of open academic data
text: analysis focuses monitoring periods 2020–2023. corresponding monitorings published data stories, available (link corresponding GitHub repository dataset): Open Access 2020: 8 percentage points 2021: strongest improvement Open Access-share yet OA monitoring 2022: strong increase continued demand article funding OA monitoring 2023: high level maintained CC licences becoming widespread. aim analysis evaluate current databases coverage SNSF‑funded publications (.e. January 2026), rely datasets used original OA monitorings. Instead, updated data SNSF-funded publications querying sources. Using updated datasets offers several advantages, including inclusion publication corrections, metadata updates enrichments, ongoing curation improvements applied databases since original monitorings. code loads datasets1 publications marked funded SNSF published 2020 2023, found OpenAlex, Dimensions, Crossref. also loads publications SNSF Data Portal dataset period. datasets generated using get_snsf_work_*() family functions period = 2020:2023. Note however using get_snsf_work_dim() get works Dimensions, API key required access API. Although analysis use datasets earlier OA monitorings available Github, still compare data updated datasets. following code retrieves past monitoring datasets using get_snsf_oa_work(). next code chunk creates two data frames: one past monitorings data one updated publication records. comparing DOIs, see : 2020–2023 OA monitorings dataset 56639 unique DOIs updated records 60905 unique DOIs 53222 already present earlier monitorings 7683 newly identified publications
code: # Load the dataset with SNSF-funded publications published in 2020-2023 and # available in the SNSF Data Portal. dp_snsf_works <- snsf.oa.ror.zurich.26::dp_snsf_works |>   arrange(doi, dp_id, dp_publication_year, dp_type) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) # Load the dataset with SNSF-funded publications published in 2020-2023 and # available in OpenAlex. oax_snsf_works <- snsf.oa.ror.zurich.26::oax_snsf_works |>   arrange(doi, oax_id, oax_publication_year, oax_type) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) # Load the dataset with SNSF-funded publications published in 2020-2023 and # available in Dimensions dim_snsf_works <- snsf.oa.ror.zurich.26::dim_snsf_works |>   arrange(doi, dim_id, dim_publication_year, dim_type) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) # Load the dataset with SNSF-funded publications published in 2020-2023 and # available in Crossref cr_snsf_works <- snsf.oa.ror.zurich.26::cr_snsf_works |>   arrange(doi, cr_publication_year, cr_type) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) |>   # For unknwon reason, there is a single publication that slipped in which has   # a publication year being 2025!   dplyr::filter(cr_publication_year %in% 2020:2023) # Read data for 2020 directly from the corresponding Github repository dat_2020 <- get_snsf_oa_work(   "datastory_new_figures_oa_monitoring_2020",   "publications_2020_dec_2021.csv" ) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Read data for 2021 directly from the corresponding Github repository and add # a flag when a DOI was already included in a earlier monitoring. dat_2021 <- get_snsf_oa_work(   "datastory_oa_monitoring_2021",   "publications_2021_mar_2023.csv" ) |>   mutate(in_past_monitoring = doi %in% dat_2020[["doi"]]) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Read data for 2022 directly from the corresponding Github repository and add # a flag when a DOI was already included in a earlier monitoring. dat_2022 <- get_snsf_oa_work(   "datastory_open_access_publications_monitoring_2022",   "publications_2022_feb_2024.csv" ) |>   mutate(     in_past_monitoring = doi %in% c(dat_2020[["doi"]], dat_2021[["doi"]])   ) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE)  # Read data for 2023 directly from the corresponding Github repository and add # a flag when a DOI was already included in a earlier monitoring. dat_2023 <- get_snsf_oa_work(   "datastory_open_access_publications_monitoring_2023",   "publications_2023_mar_2025.csv" ) |>   mutate(     in_past_monitoring = doi %in%       c(         dat_2020[["doi"]],         dat_2021[["doi"]],         dat_2022[["doi"]]       )   ) |>   distinct(doi, .keep_all = TRUE) # Combine all SNSF OA monitorings into a single data frame all_snsf_oa <- bind_rows(dat_2020, dat_2021, dat_2022, dat_2023)  # Counting the number of unique DOIs and DOIs identified in a earlier # monitoring. snsf_oa_unique_dois <- all_snsf_oa |>   distinct(doi, in_past_monitoring) |>   mutate(in_past_monitoring = replace_na(in_past_monitoring, FALSE)) |>   count(in_past_monitoring)  # Combine the updated records from all sources into a single data frame all_updated_publications <- list(   dp_snsf_works,   oax_snsf_works,   dim_snsf_works,   cr_snsf_works ) |>   reduce(\(x, y) full_join(x, y, by = join_by(doi))) |>   drop_na(doi) |>   dplyr::filter()

code: # The final dataset with only unique publications all_publications_clean_year <- all_updated_publications |>   # Row-by-row, we create a new variable with the oldest publication year for   # each publications (it may vary across sources).   rowwise() |>   mutate(     publication_year = min(       c(         dp_publication_year,         oax_publication_year,         dim_publication_year,         cr_publication_year       ),       na.rm = TRUE     )   ) |>   ungroup() |>   mutate(     in_dp = !is.na(dp_id),     in_oax = !is.na(oax_id),     in_dim = !is.na(dim_id),     in_cr = !is.na(cr_type),   ) |>   select(doi, publication_year, starts_with("in_"))

title: Monitoring open access publications at the SNSF: Challenges of open academic data
text: analysis shows monitoring open access SNSF-funded publications requires combination open closed academic databases. Even though using open academic databases Crossref OpenAlex promotes transparency, reproducibility, accessibility, currently enough access largest part SNSF-funded publications. Indeed, since Dimensions includes unique outputs captured elsewhere Dimensions, still enough rely solely data, combined publications SNSF Data Portal, conduct OA monitoring. main challenge lack widely adopted standard funding metadata. practice, many authors continue report funding information unstructured text within acknowledgements, rather using structured metadata. inconsistency limits discoverability funded research open databases makes difficult build reliable open monitoring systems.
